assumptions: SELECTION RULE (geometry only, fixed before any image was traced or matched): for every traverse.json waypoint compute the DTM horizon (40 m steps, 2 deg azimuth, as skyline.py) and, per azimuth, where the horizon-forming terrain lies. An azimuth is 'good' if the horizon is 0.5-8 deg above level (visible in a horizon strip with mastEl near 0) AND the forming terrain is >= 1 km inside the DTM bounds AND <= 14 km away (inside the 15 km range the matcher uses). Every 96 deg window is scored by its fraction of good azimuths; ranked: single-waypoint sols first, then fraction (0.01), then std of the DTM horizon elevation (more relief = more to match). Code: screen() in this script.

Frame rule: first candidate in rank order with one full-width (5120 px) frame, mastEl within +-8 deg, LTST 9-16 h, true azimuth (rover heading from the attitude quaternion + camera_vector) within +-15 deg of the window centre; earliest frame at that pointing. Candidates examined: 7; skipped: 1 sol 1175 (window 62-158): horizon strips exist but their true azimuths (72, 144) are 34-38 deg from the window centre; other frames are tilted (mastEl +25 or <-3) or half-field | 2 sol 1117 (124-220): only horizon strip points at true azimuth 355 | 3 sol 1101 (130-226): only half-width (2576 px) horizon strips at azimuths 21, 67, 287, 333 | 4 sol 1063 (132-228): no horizon strip (all frames mastEl < -25) | 5 sol 1814 (76-172): no single full-width frame near mastEl 0 (only 2576 px half-field tiles) | 6 sol 1102 (130-226): only horizon strip points at true azimuth 355 | 7 sol 1946 (232-328): full-width strip at true azimuth 288, LTST 11:12, mastEl -3.7 -> used.
Frames tried: 1. Edge-detector settings tried: 1 (sigma 1.5 px, step threshold 4.0 grey levels/px), identical to test 1; no tuning.

Frame is a full-width strip: subframeRect (1,1025,5120,1408) of the 5120x3840 detector, scaleFactor 4, delivered as 1280x352 px; horizon band only. Overlay checked once: the trace follows the visible skyline along its whole length; rover hardware appears only at the bottom edge, far from the skyline.

Optics from the frame's own CAHVORE model (fisheye type, radial terms R used, entrance-pupil term E ignored): principal point hc=648, vc=229 in the delivered strip's pixel coordinates, focal ~740 px; field across the strip 96 deg wide.
Rover tilt is included through the attitude quaternion; camera_vector/mastAz are rover-frame, so true azimuth = rover heading + mastAz.

Convention fixed independently of any skyline fit: bearing test on the traverse: for 20 sols where traverse.json shows a drive >60 m since the previous waypoint, the yaw of the last frame's quaternion read as rover->site matched the drive bearing better than the opposite reading in 15 of 20 sols (in 5 sols it was within 12 deg of the drive bearing while the opposite reading was off by 110-157 deg), i.e. the rover mostly drives forward along its heading; no skyline data involved (one-off check run outside this script on 20 sols). Other reading shown side by side: boresight azimuth 179 deg -> fitted RMS 2.41 deg, grid error 2970 m / uncertainty 922 m.
Position truth = traverse.json waypoint for this sol (sol-level, not the exact imaging position; accuracy tens of metres or worse).

Grid search: same 61x61 / 100 m grid and RMS/uncertainty rules as skyline.py, centred on a seeded prior 1-2 km from the waypoint; heading free only within +-10 deg of the nominal azimuth; no elevation offset allowed (a free-offset variant is also reported).
Fraction of the traced azimuths whose DTM-horizon terrain is >= 1 km inside the DTM and <= 14 km away: 1.00.
DTM is 20 m CTX; it cannot contain metre-scale rocks and ridges near the rover, which appear in the photo's skyline.
Skyline = first strong bright-to-dark step from the top; columns without an edge or deviating >12 px from a running median are dropped; 5-px median smoothing; resampled onto the 2 deg azimuth grid.
method: Real Navcam frame (NASA/JPL-Caltech raw image), skyline traced and matched against the CTX DTM horizon; single image, hand-tuned edge detection; not simulated.
verdict: POOR match: unfitted RMS at the waypoint 1.01 deg; fitted RMS 0.52 deg with elevation offset +0.84 deg and azimuth shift -7.00 deg. Grid search (+-3 km, 100 m, heading +-10 deg): 1263 m from the waypoint, uncertainty radius 1965 m; with a free elevation offset 946 m / 1556 m. 100% of the traced azimuths have their DTM-horizon terrain inside the DTM. This frame does NOT support the claim that a position fix of tens of metres is achievable from a single real photo. Not a statistical result.
